Updates the Tantivy index incrementally.\n27\t\n28\t### Usage\n29\t\n30\t```\n31\tagentscribe scrape [options]\n32\t```\n33\t\n34\t### Options\n35\t\n36\t| Option | Short | Default | Description |\n37\t|--------|-------|---------|-------------|\n38\t| `--plugin <name>` | `-p` | all plugins | Scrape only the named plugin. Can be repeated (`-p claude-code -p aider`). |\n39\t| `--project <path>` | | all projects | Scrape only sessions from the given project directory. Matches against the session's `project` field. |\n40\t| `--file <path>` | | | Scrape a single source file. Useful for testing a plugin against one log file. Requires `--plugin`. |\n41\t| `--dry-run` | `-n` | off | Show what would be scraped without writing any files or updating the index. |\n42\t| `--output-events` | | off | With `--dry-run`, print each parsed event as a JSON object to stdout. Use to verify field mapping. |\n43\t| `--force` | `-f` | off | Ignore scrape state (last-seen offsets) and re-scrape everything. Does not delete existing sessions — deduplicates by session ID. |\n44\t| `--no-index` | | off | Write session files but skip Tantivy index update. Useful for bulk imports where you'll `index rebuild` afterward. |\n45\t| `--since <datetime>` | | | Only scrape sessions with activity after this timestamp. ISO 8601 or relative (`24h`, `7d`, `1w`). |\n46\t\n47\t### Examples\n48\t\n49\t```bash\n50\t# Scrape all configured plugins\n51\tagentscribe scrape\n52\t\n53\t# Scrape only Claude Code sessions\n54\tagentscribe scrape --plugin claude-code\n55\t\n56\t# Dry-run with event output to verify a new plugin\n57\tagentscribe scrape --plugin pilot --dry-run --output-events\n58\t\n59\t# Scrape a single file for debugging\n60\tagentscribe scrape --plugin aider --file ~/myproject/.aider.chat.history.md\n61\t\n62\t# Re-scrape everything from scratch\n63\tagentscribe scrape --force\n64\t\n65\t# Bulk import without indexing (rebuild index after)\n66\tagentscribe scrape --force --no-index\n67\tagentscribe index rebuild\n68\t```\n69\t\n70\t### Output\n71\t\n72\tHuman-readable (default):\n73\t```\n74\tScraping claude-code...\n75\t  Found 12 new sessions (skipped 89 unchanged)\n76\t  Wrote 12 session files to ~/.agentscribe/sessions/claude-code/\n77\tScraping aider...\n78\t  Found 3 new sessions (skipped 5 unchanged)\n79\t  Wrote 3 session files to ~/.agentscribe/sessions/aider/\n80\tIndex updated: 15 documents added (1,262 total)\n81\t```\n82\t\n83\tJSON (`--json`):\n84\t```json\n85\t{\n86\t  \"plugins\": [\n87\t    {\n88\t      \"name\": \"claude-code\",\n89\t      \"new_sessions\": 12,\n90\t      \"skipped_sessions\": 89,\n91\t      \"errors\": []\n92\t    },\n93\t    {\n94\t      \"name\": \"aider\",\n95\t      \"new_sessions\": 3,\n96\t      \"skipped_sessions\": 5,\n97\t      \"errors\": []\n98\t    }\n99\t  ],\n100\t  \"index\": {\n101\t    \"documents_added\": 15,\n102\t    \"total_documents\": 1262\n103\t  }\n104\t}\n105\t```\n106\t\n107\t### Exit Codes\n108\t\n109\t| Code | Meaning |\n110\t|------|---------|\n111\t| 0 | Success — all plugins scraped without errors |\n112\t| 1 | Partial failure — some plugins had errors, others succeeded. Check `errors` in JSON output. |\n113\t| 2 | Total failure — no sessions scraped. Likely a config or permissions issue. |\n114\t\n115\t---\n116\t\n117\t## `agentscribe search`\n118\t\n119\tQuery the Tantivy index for matching sessions. The primary interface for agents seeking past solutions.\n120\t\n121\t### Usage\n122\t\n123\t```\n124\tagentscribe search <query> [options]\n125\t```\n126\t\n127\t### Arguments\n128\t\n129\t| Argument | Required | Description |\n130\t|----------|----------|-------------|\n131\t| `<query>` | no* | Search query string. Supports Tantivy query syntax: `+required -excluded \"exact phrase\"`, field-scoped queries (`content:migration`), boolean operators (`AND`, `OR`, `NOT`), fuzzy terms (`migrat~1`), wildcard (`migrat*`). Required unless using `--error`, `--code`, `--solution-only`, `--like`, or `--session`. |\n132\t\n133\t### Options\n134\t\n135\t| Option | Short | Default | Description |\n136\t|--------|-------|---------|-------------|\n137\t| `--error <pattern>` | | | Search error fingerprints. Matches against normalized error patterns (e.g., `ConnectionError:Connection refused`). |\n138\t| `--code <query>` | | | Search extracted code artifacts by content. |\n139\t| `--lang <language>` | | | Language filter for `--code` search (e.g., `rust`, `python`, `typescript`). |\n140\t| `--solution-only` | | off | Return only sessions that have an extracted solution. |\n141\t| `--like <session-id>` | | | Find sessions similar to the given session ID using TF-IDF similarity. |\n142\t| `--session <id>` | | | Retrieve a specific session by ID. Ignores query and filters. Returns the full session content. |\n143\t| `--max-results <n>` | `-n` | `10` | Maximum number of sessions to return. |\n144\t| `--snippet-length <n>` | | `200` | Maximum character length of content snippets per result. Set to `0` to omit snippets. |\n145\t| `--token-budget <n>` | | | Token budget for greedy knapsack context packing. Optimally packs results within the token limit. |\n146\t| `--agent <name>` | `-a` | all | Filter to sessions from this agent type. Can be repeated. |\n147\t| `--project <path>` | | all | Filter to sessions from this project directory. |\n148\t| `--since <datetime>` | | | Only match sessions after this timestamp. ISO 8601 or relative (`24h`, `7d`, `1w`). |\n149\t| `--before <datetime>` | | | Only match sessions before this timestamp. |\n150\t| `--tag <tag>` | `-t` | | Filter by tag. Can be repeated (AND logic). |\n151\t| `--outcome <outcome>` | | | Filter by session outcome: `success`, `failure`, `abandoned`, `unknown`. |\n152\t| `--type <type>` | | all | Filter by document type: `session`, `code_artifact`. |\n153\t| `--model <name>` | | all | Filter by LLM model name. |\n154\t| `--sort <field>` | `-s` | `relevance` | Sort order: `relevance` (BM25 score), `newest`, `oldest`, `turns`. |\n155\t| `--offset <n>` | | `0` | Skip first N results. For pagination. |\n156\t| `--fuzzy` | | off | Enable fuzzy matching on all query terms (Levenshtein distance 1). Useful when agents don't know exact terminology. |\n157\t\n158\t### Examples\n159\t\n160\t```bash\n161\t# Basic search\n162\tagentscribe search \"postgres migration\"\n163\t\n164\t# Agent-oriented: JSON output, limited results, short snippets\n165\tagentscribe search \"database connection timeout\" --json -n 3 --snippet-length 150\n166\t\n167\t# Scoped to a specific agent and project\n168\tagentscribe search \"deploy\" --agent claude-code --project /home/coding/myapp\n169\t\n170\t# Recent sessions only\n171\tagentscribe search \"build failure\" --since 7d\n172\t\n173\t# Fuzzy search for misspellings or approximate terms\n174\tagentscribe search \"kuberntes\" --fuzzy\n175\t\n176\t# Exact phrase search\n177\tagentscribe search '\"connection pool exhausted\"'\n178\t\n179\t# Advanced Tantivy query syntax\n180\tagentscribe search '+content:migration +agent:claude-code -content:rollback'\n181\t\n182\t# Retrieve a specific session's full content\n183\tagentscribe search --session claude-code/83f5a4e7\n184\t\n185\t# Search by error fingerprint\n186\tagentscribe search --error \"ConnectionError\"\n187\t\n188\t# Search code artifacts\n189\tagentscribe search --code \"fn migrate\" --lang rust\n190\t\n191\t# Find sessions with extracted solutions\n192\tagentscribe search \"auth token\" --solution-only\n193\t\n194\t# Find similar sessions\n195\tagentscribe search --like claude-code/83f5a4e7\n196\t\n197\t# Context packing for agent prompts (fit within token budget)\n198\tagentscribe search \"error handling\" --token-budget 4000 --json\n199\t\n200\t# Filter by document type and model\n201\tagentscribe search \"refactor\" --type code_artifact --model claude-sonnet-4-20250514\n202\t```\n203\t\n204\t### Output\n205\t\n206\tHuman-readable (default):\n207\t```\n208\t3 results for \"postgres migration\" (searched 1,262 sessions in 4ms)\n209\t\n210\t[1] claude-code/83f5a4e7  (score: 8.42)\n211\t    Project:  /home/coding/myapp\n212\t    Date:     2026-03-14 10:30\n213\t    Turns:    42\n214\t    Outcome:  success\n215\t    Summary:  Migrated Postgres schema from v3 to v4, added rollback script\n216\t    Snippet:  ...ran ALTER TABLE to add the new columns, then backfilled\n217\t              existing rows. The migration took 3 minutes on a 2M row table...\n218\t\n219\t[2] aider/session-2026-03-10  (score: 6.18)\n220\t    Project:  /home/coding/api-server\n221\t    Date:     2026-03-10 14:15\n222\t    Turns:    18\n223\t    Outcome:  success\n224\t    Summary:  Fixed Postgres connection pooling, added retry logic\n225\t    Snippet:  ...the connection pool was exhausting under load because\n226\t              max_connections was set to 10. Bumped to 50 and added...\n227\t\n228\t[3] codex/abc-thread-123  (score: 4.01)\n229\t    Project:  /home/coding/data-pipeline\n230\t    Date:     2026-03-08 09:00\n231\t    Turns:    7\n232\t    Outcome:  failure\n233\t    Summary:  Attempted Postgres 14->16 upgrade, hit extension incompatibility\n234\t    Snippet:  ...pg_trgm extension not available in pg16 container image.\n235\t              Rolled back to pg14 and opened an issue...\n236\t```\n237\t\n238\tJSON (`--json`):\n239\t```json\n240\t{\n241\t  \"query\": \"postgres migration\",\n242\t  \"total_matches\": 3,\n243\t  \"search_time_ms\": 4,\n244\t  \"sessions_searched\": 1262,\n245\t  \"results\": [\n246\t    {\n247\t      \"session_id\": \"claude-code/83f5a4e7\",\n248\t      \"source_agent\": \"claude-code\",\n249\t      \"project\": \"/home/coding/myapp\",\n250\t      \"timestamp\": \"2026-03-14T10:30:00Z\",\n251\t      \"turns\": 42,\n252\t      \"outcome\": \"success\",\n253\t      \"score\": 8.42,\n254\t      \"summary\": \"Migrated Postgres schema from v3 to v4, added rollback script\",\n255\t      \"snippet\": \"...ran ALTER TABLE to add the new columns, then backfilled existing rows. The migration took 3 minutes on a 2M row table...\",\n256\t      \"tags\": [\"postgres\", \"migration\", \"schema\", \"alter-table\"]\n257\t    }\n258\t  ]\n259\t}\n260\t```\n261\t\n262\t### Search --json Output Schema\n263\t\n264\t> **Stability contract.** The `--json` output is a stable, machine-readable\n265\t> contract relied on by NEEDLE Phase 4, MCP tool callers, and shell hooks.\n266\t> Fields **may be added** in any release. Existing fields are **never renamed,\n267\t> removed, or retyped** without a major version bump. Callers should ignore\n268\t> unknown keys so additive changes do not break them.\n269\t\n270\tOutput is a single pretty-printed JSON object (`serde_json::to_string_pretty`,\n271\t2-space indent) printed to stdout. The same shape is returned by the MCP\n272\t`search` tool, which wraps the same `execute_search` call via\n273\t`serde_json::to_value`, so CLI and MCP callers can share one parser.\n274\t\n275\tThe shape is locked by `tests/search_contract.rs`, which fails the build if a\n276\tfield is renamed, removed, or retyped without updating both the code and the\n277\ttest.\n278\t\n279\t**Envelope** (`SearchOutput`):\n280\t\n281\t| Field | JSON type | Presence |\n282\t|-------|-----------|----------|\n283\t| `query` | string | Always present. May be empty `\"\"` when only a filter (`--agent`, `--tag`, …) was supplied. |\n284\t| `total_matches` | integer | Always present. Equal to `results.length`. |\n285\t| `search_time_ms` | integer | Always present. Wall-clock duration of the search, in milliseconds. |\n286\t| `sessions_searched` | integer | Always present. Number of documents in the index when the search ran. |\n287\t| `results` | array of result objects | Always present. May be empty `[]` — zero matches is a valid result, not an error. |\n288\t| `fuzzy_fallback` | boolean | **Conditional.** Omitted when `false`; present and `true` only when a plain query returned zero hits and an automatic fuzzy retry produced results. |\n289\t\n290\t**Result object** (`SearchResult` — each entry of `results`):\n291\t\n292\t| Field | JSON type | Nullability |\n293\t|-------|-----------|-------------|\n294\t| `session_id` | string | Always present. May be `\"\"` if the indexed document carried no id. |\n295\t| `source_agent` | string | Always present. E.g. `claude-code`, `aider`, `codex`. |\n296\t| `project` | string | Nullable — `null` when the session had no project. |\n297\t| `timestamp` | string (RFC 3339) | Nullable — `null` when no timestamp was recorded. Format e.g. `\"2026-03-14T10:30:00+00:00\"`. |\n298\t| `turns` | integer | Nullable — `null` when turn count was not recorded. |\n299\t| `outcome` | string | Nullable — `null` when unset; otherwise e.g. `success`, `failure`, `abandoned`. |\n300\t| `score` | number (float) | Always present. BM25 relevance, RRF fusion score, or cosine similarity depending on mode (`--semantic` / `--hybrid`). **Note:** `--semantic` and `--hybrid` modes are currently non-functional stub implementations — they return dummy similarity scores. Range is not contractually bounded. |\n301\t| `summary` | string | Nullable — `null` when the session had no summary. |\n302\t| `snippet` | string | Nullable — `null` when no snippet was extracted (e.g. `--snippet-length 0` or empty content). May be truncated and end with `...`. |\n303\t| `tags` | array of strings | Always present. May be empty `[]`; never omitted. |\n304\t| `doc_type` | string | Nullable — `null` when unset; otherwise e.g. `session` or `code_artifact`. |\n305\t| `model` | string | Nullable — `null` when the model was not recorded. |\n306\t| `token_count` | integer | Always present (≥ 0). Estimated as `ceil((snippet_chars + summary_chars) / 4)`. |\n307\t\n308\tNotes for callers:\n309\t\n310\t- Apart from `fuzzy_fallback` (omitted when `false`), every field above is\n311\t  **always present** in its object — optional fields appear as `null`, never\n312\t  disappear. This means a parser can read them by name unconditionally.\n313\t- Object key order matches the struct definition order shown above, but key\n314\t  order is **not** part of the contract — look fields up by name, never by\n315\t  position.\n316\t- Numbers serialize as JSON numbers; integers have no fractional part. `score`\n317\t  is the only field that may carry a fractional component.\n318\t\n319\t### Full Session Retrieval\n320\t\n321\tWhen `--session <id>` is used, returns the complete normalized conversation:\n322\t\n323\t```bash\n324\tagentscribe search --session claude-code/83f5a4e7 --json\n325\t```\n326\t\n327\t```json\n328\t{\n329\t  \"session_id\": \"claude-code/83f5a4e7\",\n330\t  \"source_agent\": \"claude-code\",\n331\t  \"project\": \"/home/coding/myapp\",\n332\t  \"started\": \"2026-03-14T10:30:00Z\",\n333\t  \"ended\": \"2026-03-14T11:15:00Z\",\n334\t  \"turns\": 42,\n335\t  \"outcome\": \"success\",\n336\t  \"summary\": \"Migrated Postgres schema from v3 to v4, added rollback script\",\n337\t  \"events\": [\n338\t    {\n339\t      \"ts\": \"2026-03-14T10:30:00Z\",\n340\t      \"role\": \"user\",\n341\t      \"content\": \"I need to migrate the Postgres schema from v3 to v4...\"\n342\t    },\n343\t    {\n344\t      \"ts\": \"2026-03-14T10:30:15Z\",\n345\t      \"role\": \"assistant\",\n346\t      \"content\": \"I'll create a migration script that...\"\n347\t    }\n348\t  ]\n349\t}\n350\t```\n351\t\n352\t### Exit Codes\n353\t\n354\t| Code | Meaning |\n355\t|------|---------|\n356\t| 0 | Results found |\n357\t| 0 | No results (empty results array, not an error) |\n358\t| 1 | Query parse error or invalid filter |\n359\t| 2 | Index not found — run `agentscribe scrape` first |\n360\t\n361\t---\n362\t\n363\t## `agentscribe index`\n364\t\n365\tManage the Tantivy search index.\n366\t\n367\t### Usage\n368\t\n369\t```\n370\tagentscribe index <subcommand> [options]\n371\t```\n372\t\n373\t### Subcommands\n374\t\n375\t#### `agentscribe index rebuild`\n376\t\n377\tDrop the existing Tantivy index and rebuild it from all normalized session files. Use after a bulk import, after changing the schema, or to recover from index corruption.\n378\t\n379\t| Option | Short | Default | Description |\n380\t|--------|-------|---------|-------------|\n381\t| `--plugin <name>` | `-p` | all | Only re-index sessions from this plugin. |\n382\t| `--heap-size <mb>` | | `50` | Tantivy writer heap size in MB. Higher = faster indexing, more RAM. |\n383\t\n384\t```bash\n385\t# Full rebuild\n386\tagentscribe index rebuild\n387\t\n388\t# Rebuild only Claude Code sessions\n389\tagentscribe index rebuild --plugin claude-code\n390\t\n391\t# Fast rebuild with more memory\n392\tagentscribe index rebuild --heap-size 100\n393\t```\n394\t\n395\tOutput:\n396\t```\n397\tDropping existing index...\n398\tRebuilding from 1,262 session files...\n399\t  [========================================] 1262/1262 (47/s)\n400\tIndex rebuilt in 26.8s\n401\t```\n402\t\n403\t#### `agentscribe index stats`\n404\t\n405\tShow index statistics.\n406\t\n407\t```bash\n408\tagentscribe index stats\n409\t```\n410\t\n411\tOutput:\n412\t```\n413\tTantivy index at ~/.agentscribe/index/tantivy/\n414\t  Documents:    1,262\n415\t  Segments:     4\n416\t  Size on disk: 38 MB\n417\t  Last updated: 2026-03-16 12:30:00\n418\t  Fields:       content, summary, session_id, source_agent, project, tags, timestamp, turn_count, outcome\n419\t```\n420\t\n421\tJSON (`--json`):\n422\t```json\n423\t{\n424\t  \"path\": \"~/.agentscribe/index/tantivy/\",\n425\t  \"documents\": 1262,\n426\t  \"segments\": 4,\n427\t  \"size_bytes\": 39845888,\n428\t  \"last_updated\": \"2026-03-16T12:30:00Z\",\n429\t  \"fields\": [\"content\", \"summary\", \"session_id\", \"source_agent\", \"project\", \"tags\", \"timestamp\", \"turn_count\", \"outcome\"]\n430\t}\n431\t```\n432\t\n433\t#### `agentscribe index optimize`\n434\t\n435\tForce-merge Tantivy segments for better query performance. Normally unnecessary — Tantivy auto-merges in the background.\n436\t\n437\t```bash\n438\tagentscribe index optimize\n439\t```\n440\t\n441\tOutput:\n442\t```\n443\tMerging 4 segments into 1... done (3.2s)\n444\tIndex size: 38 MB -> 35 MB\n445\t```\n446\t\n447\t### Exit Codes\n448\t\n449\t| Code | Meaning |\n450\t|------|---------|\n451\t| 0 | Success |\n452\t| 1 | Index error (corruption, missing session files) |\n453\t| 2 | No session files found — run `agentscribe scrape` first |\n454\t\n455\t---\n456\t\n457\t## `agentscribe status`\n458\t\n459\tShow a summary of what AgentScribe daemon that watches for new log data and scrapes automatically.\n537\t\n538\t### Usage\n539\t\n540\t```\n541\tagentscribe daemon <subcommand> [options]\n542\t```\n543\t\n544\t### Subcommands\n545\t\n546\t#### `agentscribe daemon start`\n547\t\n548\tStart the daemon in the background. Writes PID to `~/.agentscribe/agentscribe.pid`. Logs to `~/.agentscribe/daemon.log`.\n549\t\n550\t| Option | Short | Default | Description |\n551\t|--------|-------|---------|-------------|\n552\t| `--mcp` | | off | Enable MCP server on the daemon. Listens on a Unix socket at `~/.agentscribe/mcp.sock`. |\n553\t| `--log-level <level>` | | `info` | Daemon log level: `error`, `warn`, `info`, `debug`, `trace`. |\n554\t| `--scrape-debounce <duration>` | | `5s` | Wait this long after a file change before scraping. Prevents thrashing during active agent sessions. |\n555\t\n556\t```bash\n557\t# Start with defaults\n558\tagentscribe daemon start\n559\t\n560\t# Start with MCP server enabled\n561\tagentscribe daemon start --mcp\n562\t\n563\t# Start with debug logging\n564\tagentscribe daemon start --log-level debug\n565\t```\n566\t\n567\tOutput:\n568\t```\n569\tAgentScribe daemon started (PID 12345)\n570\t  Watching: 4 plugin source paths\n571\t  MCP: disabled\n572\t  Log: ~/.agentscribe/daemon.log\n573\t```\n574\t\n575\t#### `agentscribe daemon stop`\n576\t\n577\tStop the running daemon. Sends SIGTERM and waits for clean shutdown.\n578\t\n579\t| Option | Short | Default | Description |\n580\t|--------|-------|---------|-------------|\n581\t| `--force` | | off | Send SIGKILL if the daemon doesn't stop within 5 seconds. |\n582\t\n583\t```bash\n584\tagentscribe daemon stop\n585\t```\n586\t\n587\tOutput:\n588\t```\n589\tStopping AgentScribe daemon (PID 12345)... stopped.\n590\t```\n591\t\n592\t#### `agentscribe daemon status`\n593\t\n594\tShow daemon state, resource usage, and activity.\n595\t\n596\t```bash\n597\tagentscribe daemon status\n598\t```\n599\t\n600\tOutput:\n601\t```\n602\tAgentScribe daemon (PID 12345)\n603\t  Status:     running\n604\t  Uptime:     3d 14h\n605\t  RSS:        12 MB\n606\t  Peak RSS:   47 MB\n607\t  MCP:        disabled\n608\t  Log:        ~/.agentscribe/daemon.log\n609\t\n610\t  Watches:    4 paths\n611\t  Last scrape: 2m ago (3 new sessions from claude-code)\n612\t  Total scrapes: 847 since start\n613\t  Errors:     0\n614\t```\n615\t\n616\tJSON (`--json`):\n617\t```json\n618\t{\n619\t  \"pid\": 12345,\n620\t  \"status\": \"running\",\n621\t  \"uptime_seconds\": 309600,\n622\t  \"rss_bytes\": 12582912,\n623\t  \"peak_rss_bytes\": 49283072,\n624\t  \"mcp_enabled\": false,\n625\t  \"log_path\": \"~/.agentscribe/daemon.log\",\n626\t  \"watches\": 4,\n627\t  \"last_scrape\": \"2026-03-16T12:28:00Z\",\n628\t  \"last_scrape_new_sessions\": 3,\n629\t  \"total_scrapes\": 847,\n630\t  \"errors\": 0\n631\t}\n632\t```\n633\t\n634\t#### `agentscribe daemon run`\n635\t\n636\tRun the daemon in the foreground. Use this when managing the process via systemd, supervisord, or similar. Does not daemonize, does not write a PID file. Logs to stderr.\n637\t\n638\t| Option | Short | Default | Description |\n639\t|--------|-------|---------|-------------|\n640\t| `--mcp` | | off | Enable MCP server. |\n641\t| `--log-level <level>` | | `info` | Log level. |\n642\t| `--scrape-debounce <duration>` | | `5s` | Debounce period. |\n643\t\n644\t```bash\n645\t# Foreground (for systemd)\n646\tagentscribe daemon run\n647\t\n648\t# With MCP and debug logging\n649\tagentscribe daemon run --mcp --log-level debug\n650\t```\n651\t\n652\t#### `agentscribe daemon logs`\n653\t\n654\tTail the daemon log file. Convenience wrapper for reading `~/.agentscribe/daemon.log`.\n655\t\n656\t| Option | Short | Default | Description |\n657\t|--------|-------|---------|-------------|\n658\t| `--follow` | `-f` | off | Follow new output (like `tail -f`). |\n659\t| `--lines <n>` | `-n` | `50` | Number of lines to show. |\n660\t| `--level <level>` | | all | Filter to this log level or above. |\n661\t\n662\t```bash\n663\t# Last 50 lines\n664\tagentscribe daemon logs\n665\t\n666\t# Follow in real time\n667\tagentscribe daemon logs -f\n668\t\n669\t# Only errors\n670\tagentscribe daemon logs --level error -n 100\n671\t```\n672\t\n673\t### Exit Codes\n674\t\n675\t| Code | Meaning |\n676\t|------|---------|\n677\t| 0 | Success |\n678\t| 1 | Daemon not running (for `stop`, `status`) or failed to start |\n679\t| 2 | PID file exists but process is dead (stale PID) — cleaned up automatically |\n680\t\n681\t---\n682\t\n683\t## `agentscribe plugins`\n684\t\n685\tManage scraper plugin (Phase 3 feature.)\n938\t\n939\t### Usage\n940\t\n941\t```\n942\tagentscribe summarize <session-id> [options]\n943\t```\n944\t\n945\t### Arguments\n946\t\n947\t| Argument | Required | Description |\n948\t|----------|----------|-------------|\n949\t| `<session-id>` | yes | Session ID in `<agent>/<id>` format. |\n950\t\n951\t### Options\n952\t\n953\t| Option | Short | Default | Description |\n954\t|--------|-------|---------|-------------|\n955\t| `--force` | `-f` | off | Regenerate even if a summary already exists. |\n956\t| `--method <method>` | | `extractive` | Summarization method: `extractive` (keyword/heuristic, no external deps) or `llm` (requires configured LLM endpoint). |\n957\t| `--stdout` | | off | Print summary to stdout instead of writing to the session's `.md` file. |\n958\t\n959\t### Examples\n960\t\n961\t```bash\n962\t# Summarize a session\n963\tagentscribe summarize claude-code/83f5a4e7\n964\t\n965\t# Regenerate with LLM-powered summarization\n966\tagentscribe summarize claude-code/83f5a4e7 --force --method llm\n967\t\n968\t# Preview without writing\n969\tagentscribe summarize claude-code/83f5a4e7 --stdout\n970\t```\n971\t\n972\tOutput:\n973\t```\n974\tSummary written to ~/.agentscribe/sessions/claude-code/83f5a4e7.md\n975\t```\n976\t\n977\t### Exit Codes\n978\t\n979\t| Code | Meaning |\n980\t|------|---------|\n981\t| 0 | Success |\n982\t| 1 | Session not found |\n983\t| 2 | Summary already exists (use `--force` to overwrite) |\n984\t\n985\t---\n986\t\n987\t## `agentscribe pulse-report`\n988\t\n989\tGenerate comprehensive quarterly analytics reports from the AgentScribe index. \"computed_at\": \"2026-04-01T09:00:00Z\"\n1074\t}\n1075\t```\n1076\t\n1077\t### Exit Codes\n1078\t\n1079\t| Code | Meaning |\n1080\t|------|---------|\n1081\t| 0 | Success |\n1082\t| 1 | Invalid sessions. Shows problems that happen repeatedly, which projects they affect, and links to sessions that fixed them.\n1090\t\n1091\t### Usage\n1092\t\n1093\t```\n1094\tagentscribe recurring [options]\n1095\t```\n1096\t\n1097\t### Options\n1098\t\n1099\t| Option | Short | Default | Description |\n1100\t|--------|-------|---------|-------------|\n1101\t| `--since <datetime>` | | `30d` | Only consider sessions after this timestamp. ISO 8601 or relative (`30d`, `12w`). |\n1102\t| `--threshold <n>` | | `3` | Minimum occurrence count to report. Problems with fewer occurrences are excluded. |\n1103\t| `--json` | | off | Output in JSON format. |\n1104\t\n1105\t### Examples\n1106\t\n1107\t```bash\n1108\t# Find recurring problems in the last 30 days\n1109\tagentscribe recurring\n1110\t\n1111\t# Only problems that occurred 5+ times\n1112\tagentscribe recurring --threshold 5\n1113\t\n1114\t# Last 90 days\n1115\tagentscribe recurring --since 90d\n1116\t\n1117\t# JSON for scripting\n1118\tagentscribe recurring --since 30d --json\n1119\t```\n1120\t\n1121\t### Output\n1122\t\n1123\tHuman-readable (default):\n1124\t```\n1125\tRecurring Displays 5h and 7d rolling windows, per-model windows, burn rates, and forecasts. Supports multi-account setups (e.g., personal vs work credentials).\n1396\t\n1397\t### Usage\n1398\t\n1399\t```\n1400\tagentscribe capacity [options]\n1401\t```\n1402\t\n1403\t### Options\n1404\t\n1405\t| Option | Short | Default | Description |\n1406\t|--------|-------|---------|-------------|\n1407\t| `--account-dir <path>` | | `~/.claude` + auto-discovered `~/.claude-*` | Claude config directories to scan (each = one account). Each `█` represents ~5% (20 bars = 100%).\n1453\t\n1454\t**Source indicators:**\n1455\t- `api_cache`: Exact numbers from cached Claude Code API response (`~/.cache/claude-usage/usage.json`)\n1456\t- `jsonl_estimate`: Approximate from parsing JSONL logs (uses cost-equivalent token weighting)\n1457\t\n1458\t**Per-model windows:** Shown for 7d window when available from cached API (sonnet, opus, cowork, omelette). Not available in JSONL fallback mode.\n1459\t\n1460\t**Burn rate:** Cost-equivalent tokens per minute averaged over the last hour.\n1461\t\n1462\t**Forecast:** Minutes until the window hits 100% at current burn rate. `null` if burn rate is zero or already at 100%.\n1463\t\n1464\tJSON (`--json`):\n1465\t```json\n1466\t[\n1467\t  {\n1468\t    \"account_id\": \"claude-default\",\n1469\t    \"adapter\": \"claude\",\n1470\t    \"plan_type\": \"max\",\n1471\t    \"rate_limit_tier\": \"default_claude_max_20x\",\n1472\t    \"utilization_5h\": 24.5,\n1473\t    \"utilization_7d\": 94.2,\n1474\t    \"resets_at_5h\": \"2026-05-03T16:15:00Z\",\n1475\t    \"resets_at_7d\": \"2026-05-03T18:30:00Z\",\n1476\t    \"model_windows_7d\": [\n1477\t      {\"model\": \"sonnet\", \"utilization\": 82.0, \"resets_at\": \"2026-05-03T18:30:00Z\"},\n1478\t      {\"model\": \"opus\", \"utilization\": 91.5, \"resets_at\": \"2026-05-03T18:30:00Z\"}\n1479\t    ],\n1480\t    \"tokens_5h\": 127000,\n1481\t    \"tokens_7d\": 2840000,\n1482\t    \"turns_5h\": 127,\n1483\t    \"turns_7d\": 2840,\n1484\t    \"burn_rate_per_min\": 8450.0,\n1485\t    \"forecast_full_5h_min\": 105.0,\n1486\t    \"forecast_full_7d_min\": null,\n1487\t    \"source\": \"api_cache\",\n1488\t    \"computed_at\": \"2026-05-03T14:20:00Z\"\n1489\t  }\n1490\t]\n1491\t```\n1492\t\n1493\t### Data Sources\n1494\t\n1495\tThe capacity meter reads from two sources (in priority order):\n1496\t\n1497\t1. **Cached API response** (`~/.cache/claude-usage/usage.json`) — exact numbers matching Claude Code's `/status` output. This file is written by Claude Code when you run `/status` or check limits.\n1498\t\n1499\t2. **JSONL-based estimation** — fallback when cache is stale or missing. Parses `~/.claude/projects/*/*.jsonl` files and counts tokens using cost-equivalent weighting:\n1500\t   - Input tokens: 1.0× weight\n1501\t   - Output tokens: ~5× weight (matching API pricing ratio)\n1502\t   - Cache read tokens: ~0.1× weight\n1503\t   - Cache write tokens: ~0.25× weight\n1504\t\n1505\tThe JSONL fallback is inherently approximate because the exact weighting formula is proprietary. The cached API response should be preferred whenever available.\n1506\t\n1507\t### Account Discovery\n1508\t\n1509\tBy default, scans:\n1510\t- `~/.claude` (named \"claude-default\" in output)\n1511\t- All `~/.claude-*` directories that contain `.credentials.json`\n1512\t\n1513\tFor example, if you have `~/.claude` and `~/.claude-work`, both will be scanned and reported separately.\n1514\t\n1515\t### Exit Codes\n1516\t\n1517\t| Code | Meaning |\n1518\t|------|---------|\n1519\t| 0 | Success |\n1520\t| 1 | No Claude accounts found |\n1521\t\n1522\t---\n1523\t\n1524\t## `agentscribe context`\n1525\t\n1526\tPre-task priming query for agent workers. This is the stable data export API for external reflection tools that analyze agent behavior across sessions.\n1670\t\n1671\t### Usage\n1672\t\n1673\t```\n1674\tagentscribe reflect <subcommand> [options]\n1675\t```\n1676\t\n1677\t### Subcommands\n1678\t\n1679\t#### `agentscribe reflect sessions`\n1680\t\n1681\tExport sessions with behavioral signals, error fingerprints, and config file interactions. When combined with `--json`, outputs a stable, machine-readable schema suitable for programmatic consumption by reflection tools.\n1682\t\n1683\t```\n1684\tagentscribe reflect sessions [options]\n1685\t```\n1686\t\n1687\t##### Options\n1688\t\n1689\t| Option | Short | Default | Description |\n1690\t|--------|-------|---------|-------------|\n1691\t| `--since <datetime>` | | all | Only include sessions after this timestamp. Can be repeated. |\n1698\t| `--json` | | off | Output in stable JSON format (documented below). |\n1699\t\n1700\t##### Examples\n1701\t\n1702\t```bash\n1703\t# Export last 30 days of sessions as Updates the Tantivy index incrementally.\n\n### Usage\n\n```\nagentscribe scrape [options]\n```\n\n### Options\n\n| Option | Short | Default | Description |\n|--------|-------|---------|-------------|\n| `--plugin <name>` | `-p` | all plugins | Scrape only the named plugin. Can be repeated (`-p claude-code -p aider`). |\n| `--project <path>` | | all projects | Scrape only sessions from the given project directory. Matches against the session's `project` field. |\n| `--file <path>` | | | Scrape a single source file. Useful for testing a plugin against one log file. Requires `--plugin`. |\n| `--dry-run` | `-n` | off | Show what would be scraped without writing any files or updating the index. |\n| `--output-events` | | off | With `--dry-run`, print each parsed event as a JSON object to stdout. Use to verify field mapping. |\n| `--force` | `-f` | off | Ignore scrape state (last-seen offsets) and re-scrape everything. Does not delete existing sessions — deduplicates by session ID. |\n| `--no-index` | | off | Write session files but skip Tantivy index update. Useful for bulk imports where you'll `index rebuild` afterward. |\n| `--since <datetime>` | | | Only scrape sessions with activity after this timestamp. ISO 8601 or relative (`24h`, `7d`, `1w`). |\n\n### Examples\n\n```bash\n# Scrape all configured plugins\nagentscribe scrape\n\n# Scrape only Claude Code sessions\nagentscribe scrape --plugin claude-code\n\n# Dry-run with event output to verify a new plugin\nagentscribe scrape --plugin pilot --dry-run --output-events\n\n# Scrape a single file for debugging\nagentscribe scrape --plugin aider --file ~/myproject/.aider.chat.history.md\n\n# Re-scrape everything from scratch\nagentscribe scrape --force\n\n# Bulk import without indexing (rebuild index after)\nagentscribe scrape --force --no-index\nagentscribe index rebuild\n```\n\n### Output\n\nHuman-readable (default):\n```\nScraping claude-code...\n  Found 12 new sessions (skipped 89 unchanged)\n  Wrote 12 session files to ~/.agentscribe/sessions/claude-code/\nScraping aider...\n  Found 3 new sessions (skipped 5 unchanged)\n  Wrote 3 session files to ~/.agentscribe/sessions/aider/\nIndex updated: 15 documents added (1,262 total)\n```\n\nJSON (`--json`):\n```json\n{\n  \"plugins\": [\n    {\n      \"name\": \"claude-code\",\n      \"new_sessions\": 12,\n      \"skipped_sessions\": 89,\n      \"errors\": []\n    },\n    {\n      \"name\": \"aider\",\n      \"new_sessions\": 3,\n      \"skipped_sessions\": 5,\n      \"errors\": []\n    }\n  ],\n  \"index\": {\n    \"documents_added\": 15,\n    \"total_documents\": 1262\n  }\n}\n```\n\n### Exit Codes\n\n| Code | Meaning |\n|------|---------|\n| 0 | Success — all plugins scraped without errors |\n| 1 | Partial failure — some plugins had errors, others succeeded. Check `errors` in JSON output. |\n| 2 | Total failure — no sessions scraped. Likely a config or permissions issue. |\n\n---\n\n## `agentscribe search`\n\nQuery the Tantivy index for matching sessions. The primary interface for agents seeking past solutions.\n\n### Usage\n\n```\nagentscribe search <query> [options]\n```\n\n### Arguments\n\n| Argument | Required | Description |\n|----------|----------|-------------|\n| `<query>` | no* | Search query string. Supports Tantivy query syntax: `+required -excluded \"exact phrase\"`, field-scoped queries (`content:migration`), boolean operators (`AND`, `OR`, `NOT`), fuzzy terms (`migrat~1`), wildcard (`migrat*`). Required unless using `--error`, `--code`, `--solution-only`, `--like`, or `--session`. |\n\n### Options\n\n| Option | Short | Default | Description |\n|--------|-------|---------|-------------|\n| `--error <pattern>` | | | Search error fingerprints. Matches against normalized error patterns (e.g., `ConnectionError:Connection refused`). |\n| `--code <query>` | | | Search extracted code artifacts by content. |\n| `--lang <language>` | | | Language filter for `--code` search (e.g., `rust`, `python`, `typescript`). |\n| `--solution-only` | | off | Return only sessions that have an extracted solution. |\n| `--like <session-id>` | | | Find sessions similar to the given session ID using TF-IDF similarity. |\n| `--session <id>` | | | Retrieve a specific session by ID. Ignores query and filters. Returns the full session content. |\n| `--max-results <n>` | `-n` | `10` | Maximum number of sessions to return. |\n| `--snippet-length <n>` | | `200` | Maximum character length of content snippets per result. Set to `0` to omit snippets. |\n| `--token-budget <n>` | | | Token budget for greedy knapsack context packing. Optimally packs results within the token limit. |\n| `--agent <name>` | `-a` | all | Filter to sessions from this agent type. Can be repeated. |\n| `--project <path>` | | all | Filter to sessions from this project directory. |\n| `--since <datetime>` | | | Only match sessions after this timestamp. ISO 8601 or relative (`24h`, `7d`, `1w`). |\n| `--before <datetime>` | | | Only match sessions before this timestamp. |\n| `--tag <tag>` | `-t` | | Filter by tag. Can be repeated (AND logic). |\n| `--outcome <outcome>` | | | Filter by session outcome: `success`, `failure`, `abandoned`, `unknown`. |\n| `--type <type>` | | all | Filter by document type: `session`, `code_artifact`. |\n| `--model <name>` | | all | Filter by LLM model name. |\n| `--sort <field>` | `-s` | `relevance` | Sort order: `relevance` (BM25 score), `newest`, `oldest`, `turns`. |\n| `--offset <n>` | | `0` | Skip first N results. For pagination. |\n| `--fuzzy` | | off | Enable fuzzy matching on all query terms (Levenshtein distance 1). Useful when agents don't know exact terminology. |\n\n### Examples\n\n```bash\n# Basic search\nagentscribe search \"postgres migration\"\n\n# Agent-oriented: JSON output, limited results, short snippets\nagentscribe search \"database connection timeout\" --json -n 3 --snippet-length 150\n\n# Scoped to a specific agent and project\nagentscribe search \"deploy\" --agent claude-code --project /home/coding/myapp\n\n# Recent sessions only\nagentscribe search \"build failure\" --since 7d\n\n# Fuzzy search for misspellings or approximate terms\nagentscribe search \"kuberntes\" --fuzzy\n\n# Exact phrase search\nagentscribe search '\"connection pool exhausted\"'\n\n# Advanced Tantivy query syntax\nagentscribe search '+content:migration +agent:claude-code -content:rollback'\n\n# Retrieve a specific session's full content\nagentscribe search --session claude-code/83f5a4e7\n\n# Search by error fingerprint\nagentscribe search --error \"ConnectionError\"\n\n# Search code artifacts\nagentscribe search --code \"fn migrate\" --lang rust\n\n# Find sessions with extracted solutions\nagentscribe search \"auth token\" --solution-only\n\n# Find similar sessions\nagentscribe search --like claude-code/83f5a4e7\n\n# Context packing for agent prompts (fit within token budget)\nagentscribe search \"error handling\" --token-budget 4000 --json\n\n# Filter by document type and model\nagentscribe search \"refactor\" --type code_artifact --model claude-sonnet-4-20250514\n```\n\n### Output\n\nHuman-readable (default):\n```\n3 results for \"postgres migration\" (searched 1,262 sessions in 4ms)\n\n[1] claude-code/83f5a4e7  (score: 8.42)\n    Project:  /home/coding/myapp\n    Date:     2026-03-14 10:30\n    Turns:    42\n    Outcome:  success\n    Summary:  Migrated Postgres schema from v3 to v4, added rollback script\n    Snippet:  ...ran ALTER TABLE to add the new columns, then backfilled\n              existing rows. The migration took 3 minutes on a 2M row table...\n\n[2] aider/session-2026-03-10  (score: 6.18)\n    Project:  /home/coding/api-server\n    Date:     2026-03-10 14:15\n    Turns:    18\n    Outcome:  success\n    Summary:  Fixed Postgres connection pooling, added retry logic\n    Snippet:  ...the connection pool was exhausting under load because\n              max_connections was set to 10. Bumped to 50 and added...\n\n[3] codex/abc-thread-123  (score: 4.01)\n    Project:  /home/coding/data-pipeline\n    Date:     2026-03-08 09:00\n    Turns:    7\n    Outcome:  failure\n    Summary:  Attempted Postgres 14->16 upgrade, hit extension incompatibility\n    Snippet:  ...pg_trgm extension not available in pg16 container image.\n              Rolled back to pg14 and opened an issue...\n```\n\nJSON (`--json`):\n```json\n{\n  \"query\": \"postgres migration\",\n  \"total_matches\": 3,\n  \"search_time_ms\": 4,\n  \"sessions_searched\": 1262,\n  \"results\": [\n    {\n      \"session_id\": \"claude-code/83f5a4e7\",\n      \"source_agent\": \"claude-code\",\n      \"project\": \"/home/coding/myapp\",\n      \"timestamp\": \"2026-03-14T10:30:00Z\",\n      \"turns\": 42,\n      \"outcome\": \"success\",\n      \"score\": 8.42,\n      \"summary\": \"Migrated Postgres schema from v3 to v4, added rollback script\",\n      \"snippet\": \"...ran ALTER TABLE to add the new columns, then backfilled existing rows. The migration took 3 minutes on a 2M row table...\",\n      \"tags\": [\"postgres\", \"migration\", \"schema\", \"alter-table\"]\n    }\n  ]\n}\n```\n\n### Search --json Output Schema\n\n> **Stability contract.** The `--json` output is a stable, machine-readable\n> contract relied on by NEEDLE Phase 4, MCP tool callers, and shell hooks.\n> Fields **may be added** in any release. Existing fields are **never renamed,\n> removed, or retyped** without a major version bump. Callers should ignore\n> unknown keys so additive changes do not break them.\n\nOutput is a single pretty-printed JSON object (`serde_json::to_string_pretty`,\n2-space indent) printed to stdout. The same shape is returned by the MCP\n`search` tool, which wraps the same `execute_search` call via\n`serde_json::to_value`, so CLI and MCP callers can share one parser.\n\nThe shape is locked by `tests/search_contract.rs`, which fails the build if a\nfield is renamed, removed, or retyped without updating both the code and the\ntest.\n\n**Envelope** (`SearchOutput`):\n\n| Field | JSON type | Presence |\n|-------|-----------|----------|\n| `query` | string | Always present. May be empty `\"\"` when only a filter (`--agent`, `--tag`, …) was supplied. |\n| `total_matches` | integer | Always present. Equal to `results.length`. |\n| `search_time_ms` | integer | Always present. Wall-clock duration of the search, in milliseconds. |\n| `sessions_searched` | integer | Always present. Number of documents in the index when the search ran. |\n| `results` | array of result objects | Always present. May be empty `[]` — zero matches is a valid result, not an error. |\n| `fuzzy_fallback` | boolean | **Conditional.** Omitted when `false`; present and `true` only when a plain query returned zero hits and an automatic fuzzy retry produced results. |\n\n**Result object** (`SearchResult` — each entry of `results`):\n\n| Field | JSON type | Nullability |\n|-------|-----------|-------------|\n| `session_id` | string | Always present. May be `\"\"` if the indexed document carried no id. |\n| `source_agent` | string | Always present. E.g. `claude-code`, `aider`, `codex`. |\n| `project` | string | Nullable — `null` when the session had no project. |\n| `timestamp` | string (RFC 3339) | Nullable — `null` when no timestamp was recorded. Format e.g. `\"2026-03-14T10:30:00+00:00\"`. |\n| `turns` | integer | Nullable — `null` when turn count was not recorded. |\n| `outcome` | string | Nullable — `null` when unset; otherwise e.g. `success`, `failure`, `abandoned`. |\n| `score` | number (float) | Always present. BM25 relevance, RRF fusion score, or cosine similarity depending on mode (`--semantic` / `--hybrid`). **Note:** `--semantic` and `--hybrid` modes are currently non-functional stub implementations — they return dummy similarity scores. Range is not contractually bounded. |\n| `summary` | string | Nullable — `null` when the session had no summary. |\n| `snippet` | string | Nullable — `null` when no snippet was extracted (e.g. `--snippet-length 0` or empty content). May be truncated and end with `...`. |\n| `tags` | array of strings | Always present. May be empty `[]`; never omitted. |\n| `doc_type` | string | Nullable — `null` when unset; otherwise e.g. `session` or `code_artifact`. |\n| `model` | string | Nullable — `null` when the model was not recorded. |\n| `token_count` | integer | Always present (≥ 0). Estimated as `ceil((snippet_chars + summary_chars) / 4)`. |\n\nNotes for callers:\n\n- Apart from `fuzzy_fallback` (omitted when `false`), every field above is\n  **always present** in its object — optional fields appear as `null`, never\n  disappear. This means a parser can read them by name unconditionally.\n- Object key order matches the struct definition order shown above, but key\n  order is **not** part of the contract — look fields up by name, never by\n  position.\n- Numbers serialize as JSON numbers; integers have no fractional part. `score`\n  is the only field that may carry a fractional component.\n\n### Full Session Retrieval\n\nWhen `--session <id>` is used, returns the complete normalized conversation:\n\n```bash\nagentscribe search --session claude-code/83f5a4e7 --json\n```\n\n```json\n{\n  \"session_id\": \"claude-code/83f5a4e7\",\n  \"source_agent\": \"claude-code\",\n  \"project\": \"/home/coding/myapp\",\n  \"started\": \"2026-03-14T10:30:00Z\",\n  \"ended\": \"2026-03-14T11:15:00Z\",\n  \"turns\": 42,\n  \"outcome\": \"success\",\n  \"summary\": \"Migrated Postgres schema from v3 to v4, added rollback script\",\n  \"events\": [\n    {\n      \"ts\": \"2026-03-14T10:30:00Z\",\n      \"role\": \"user\",\n      \"content\": \"I need to migrate the Postgres schema from v3 to v4...\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"ts\": \"2026-03-14T10:30:15Z\",\n      \"role\": \"assistant\",\n      \"content\": \"I'll create a migration script that...\"\n    }\n  ]\n}\n```\n\n### Exit Codes\n\n| Code | Meaning |\n|------|---------|\n| 0 | Results found |\n| 0 | No results (empty results array, not an error) |\n| 1 | Query parse error or invalid filter |\n| 2 | Index not found — run `agentscribe scrape` first |\n\n---\n\n## `agentscribe index`\n\nManage the Tantivy search index.\n\n### Usage\n\n```\nagentscribe index <subcommand> [options]\n```\n\n### Subcommands\n\n#### `agentscribe index rebuild`\n\nDrop the existing Tantivy index and rebuild it from all normalized session files. Use after a bulk import, after changing the schema, or to recover from index corruption.\n\n| Option | Short | Default | Description |\n|--------|-------|---------|-------------|\n| `--plugin <name>` | `-p` | all | Only re-index sessions from this plugin. |\n| `--heap-size <mb>` | | `50` | Tantivy writer heap size in MB. Higher = faster indexing, more RAM. |\n\n```bash\n# Full rebuild\nagentscribe index rebuild\n\n# Rebuild only Claude Code sessions\nagentscribe index rebuild --plugin claude-code\n\n# Fast rebuild with more memory\nagentscribe index rebuild --heap-size 100\n```\n\nOutput:\n```\nDropping existing index...\nRebuilding from 1,262 session files...\n  [========================================] 1262/1262 (47/s)\nIndex rebuilt in 26.8s\n```\n\n#### `agentscribe index stats`\n\nShow index statistics.\n\n```bash\nagentscribe index stats\n```\n\nOutput:\n```\nTantivy index at ~/.agentscribe/index/tantivy/\n  Documents:    1,262\n  Segments:     4\n  Size on disk: 38 MB\n  Last updated: 2026-03-16 12:30:00\n  Fields:       content, summary, session_id, source_agent, project, tags, timestamp, turn_count, outcome\n```\n\nJSON (`--json`):\n```json\n{\n  \"path\": \"~/.agentscribe/index/tantivy/\",\n  \"documents\": 1262,\n  \"segments\": 4,\n  \"size_bytes\": 39845888,\n  \"last_updated\": \"2026-03-16T12:30:00Z\",\n  \"fields\": [\"content\", \"summary\", \"session_id\", \"source_agent\", \"project\", \"tags\", \"timestamp\", \"turn_count\", \"outcome\"]\n}\n```\n\n#### `agentscribe index optimize`\n\nForce-merge Tantivy segments for better query performance. Normally unnecessary — Tantivy auto-merges in the background.\n\n```bash\nagentscribe index optimize\n```\n\nOutput:\n```\nMerging 4 segments into 1... done (3.2s)\nIndex size: 38 MB -> 35 MB\n```\n\n### Exit Codes\n\n| Code | Meaning |\n|------|---------|\n| 0 | Success |\n| 1 | Index error (corruption, missing session files) |\n| 2 | No session files found — run `agentscribe scrape` first |\n\n---\n\n## `agentscribe status`\n\nShow a summary of what AgentScribe knows: tracked agents, session counts, last scrape time, daemon state, and disk usage.\n\n### Usage\n\n```\nagentscribe [options]\n```\n\n### Subcommands\n\n#### `agentscribe daemon start`\n\nStart the daemon in the background. Writes PID to `~/.agentscribe/agentscribe.pid`. Logs to `~/.agentscribe/daemon.log`.\n\n| Option | Short | Default | Description |\n|--------|-------|---------|-------------|\n| `--mcp` | | off | Enable MCP server on the daemon. Listens on a Unix socket at `~/.agentscribe/mcp.sock`. |\n| `--log-level <level>` | | `info` | Daemon log level: `error`, `warn`, `info`, `debug`, `trace`. |\n| `--scrape-debounce <duration>` | | `5s` | Wait this long after a file change before scraping. Prevents thrashing during active agent sessions. |\n\n```bash\n# Start with defaults\nagentscribe daemon start\n\n# Start with MCP server enabled\nagentscribe daemon start --mcp\n\n# Start with debug logging\nagentscribe daemon start --log-level debug\n```\n\nOutput:\n```\nAgentScribe daemon started (PID 12345)\n  Watching: 4 plugin source paths\n  MCP: disabled\n  Log: ~/.agentscribe/daemon.log\n```\n\n#### `agentscribe daemon stop`\n\nStop the running daemon. Sends SIGTERM and waits for clean shutdown.\n\n| Option | Short | Default | Description |\n|--------|-------|---------|-------------|\n| `--force` | | off | Send SIGKILL if the daemon doesn't stop within 5 seconds. |\n\n```bash\nagentscribe daemon stop\n```\n\nOutput:\n```\nStopping AgentScribe daemon (PID 12345)... stopped.\n```\n\n#### `agentscribe daemon status`\n\nShow daemon state, resource usage, and activity.\n\n```bash\nagentscribe daemon status\n```\n\nOutput:\n```\nAgentScribe daemon (PID 12345)\n  Status:     running\n  Uptime:     3d 14h\n  RSS:        12 MB\n  Peak RSS:   47 MB\n  MCP:        disabled\n  Log:        ~/.agentscribe/daemon.log\n\n  Watches:    4 paths\n  Last scrape: 2m ago (3 new sessions from claude-code)\n  Total scrapes: 847 since start\n  Errors:     0\n```\n\nJSON (`--json`):\n```json\n{\n  \"pid\": 12345,\n  \"status\": \"running\",\n  \"uptime_seconds\": 309600,\n  \"rss_bytes\": 12582912,\n  \"peak_rss_bytes\": 49283072,\n  \"mcp_enabled\": false,\n  \"log_path\": \"~/.agentscribe/daemon.log\",\n  \"watches\": 4,\n  \"last_scrape\": \"2026-03-16T12:28:00Z\",\n  \"last_scrape_new_sessions\": 3,\n  \"total_scrapes\": 847,\n  \"errors\": 0\n}\n```\n\n#### `agentscribe daemon run`\n\nRun the daemon in the foreground. Use this when managing the process via systemd, supervisord, or similar. Does not daemonize, does not write a PID file. logs\n\n# Follow in real time\nagentscribe daemon logs -f\n\n# Only errors\nagentscribe daemon logs --level error -n 100\n```\n\n### Exit Codes\n\n| Code | Meaning |\n|------|---------|\n| 0 | Success |\n| 1 | Daemon not running (for `stop`, `status`) or failed to start |\n| 2 | PID file exists but process is dead (stale PID) — cleaned up automatically |\n\n---\n\n## `agentscribe plugins`\n\nManage Does not delete session data or the index. |\n\n### Exit Codes\n\n| Code | Meaning |\n|------|---------|\n| 0 | Success |\n| 1 | Invalid key or value |\n| 2 | Config file not found (for `show`, `get`, `set` — run `config init` first) |\n\n---\n\n## `agentscribe summarize`\n\nGenerate or regenerate a Markdown summary for a session. (Phase 3 feature.)\n\n### Usage\n\n```\nagentscribe summarize <session-id> [options]\n```\n\n### Arguments\n\n| Argument | Required | Description |\n|----------|----------|-------------|\n| `<session-id>` | yes | Session ID in `<agent>/<id>` format. |\n\n### Options\n\n| Option | Short | Default | Description |\n|--------|-------|---------|-------------|\n| `--force` | `-f` | off | Regenerate even if a summary already exists. |\n| `--method <method>` | | `extractive` | Summarization method: `extractive` (keyword/heuristic, no external deps) or `llm` (requires configured LLM endpoint). |\n| `--stdout` | | off | Print summary to stdout instead of writing to the session's `.md` file. |\n\n### Examples\n\n```bash\n# Summarize a session\nagentscribe summarize claude-code/83f5a4e7\n\n# Regenerate with LLM-powered summarization\nagentscribe summarize claude-code/83f5a4e7 --force --method llm\n\n# Preview without writing\nagentscribe summarize claude-code/83f5a4e7 --stdout\n```\n\nOutput:\n```\nSummary written to ~/.agentscribe/sessions/claude-code/83f5a4e7.md\n```\n\n### Exit Codes\n\n| Code | Meaning |\n|------|---------|\n| 0 | Success |\n| 1 | Session not found |\n| 2 | Summary already exists (use `--force` to overwrite) |\n\n---\n\n## `agentscribe pulse-report`\n\nGenerate comprehensive quarterly analytics reports from the AgentScribe index. Displays 5h and 7d rolling windows, per-model windows, burn rates, and forecasts. Supports multi-account setups (e.g., personal vs work credentials).\n\n### Usage\n\n```\nagentscribe capacity [options]\n```\n\n### Options\n\n| Option | Short | Default | Description |\n|--------|-------|---------|-------------|\n| `--account-dir <path>` | | `~/.claude` + auto-discovered `~/.claude-*` | Claude config directories to scan (each = one account). Repeatable. |\n| `--cache-max-age <seconds>` | | `600` | Maximum age of cached `usage.json` before falling back to JSONL estimation. |\n| `--json` | `-j` | off | Output in JSON format. |\n\n### Examples\n\n```bash\n# Show capacity for all auto-discovered accounts\nagentscribe capacity\n\n# Specific account directories\nagentscribe capacity --account-dir ~/.claude --account-dir ~/.claude-work\n\n# Use cached data even if older (up to 1 hour)\nagentscribe capacity --cache-max-age 3600\n\n# JSON for programmatic access\nagentscribe capacity --json\n```\n\n### Output\n\nHuman-readable (default):\n```\nClaude Code Capacity\n\nAccount: claude-default (max / default_claude_max_20x)\n  Source: api_cache\n  5h window:   24.5%  [█████░░░░░░░░░░░░░░]  resets in 2h 15m\n  7d window:   94.2%  [████████████████████░]  resets in 4h 30m\n    sonnet        82.0%  [█████████████████░░░]\n    opus          91.5%  [███████████████████░]\n    cowork        45.0%  [████████░░░░░░░░░░░]\n  Burn rate:  8,450 tokens/min\n  Forecast:   5h full in 1h 45m\n  Turns:      127 (5h)  2,840 (7d)\n\nAccount: .claude-work (pro / default)\n  Source: jsonl_estimate\n  5h window:   67.8%  [████████████████░░░░░]  resets in 1h 30m\n  7d window:   23.4%  [█████░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░]  resets in 5d 12h\n  Burn rate:  2,100 tokens/min\n  Turns:      42 (5h)  580 (7d)\n```\n\n**Visual meter:** ASCII progress bar shows utilization percentage. Each `█` represents ~5% (20 bars = 100%).\n\n**Source indicators:**\n- `api_cache`: Exact numbers from cached Claude Code API response (`~/.cache/claude-usage/usage.json`)\n- `jsonl_estimate`: Approximate from parsing JSONL logs (uses cost-equivalent token weighting)\n\n**Per-model windows:** Shown for 7d window when available from cached API (sonnet, opus, cowork, omelette). Not available in JSONL fallback mode.\n\n**Burn rate:** Cost-equivalent tokens per minute averaged over the last hour.\n\n**Forecast:** Minutes until the window hits 100% at current burn rate. `null` if burn rate is zero or already at 100%.\n\nJSON (`--json`):\n```json\n[\n  {\n    \"account_id\": \"claude-default\",\n    \"adapter\": \"claude\",\n    \"plan_type\": \"max\",\n    \"rate_limit_tier\": \"default_claude_max_20x\",\n    \"utilization_5h\": 24.5,\n    \"utilization_7d\": 94.2,\n    \"resets_at_5h\": \"2026-05-03T16:15:00Z\",\n    \"resets_at_7d\": \"2026-05-03T18:30:00Z\",\n    \"model_windows_7d\": [\n      {\"model\": \"sonnet\", \"utilization\": 82.0, \"resets_at\": \"2026-05-03T18:30:00Z\"},\n      {\"model\": \"opus\", \"utilization\": 91.5, \"resets_at\": \"2026-05-03T18:30:00Z\"}\n    ],\n    \"tokens_5h\": 127000,\n    \"tokens_7d\": 2840000,\n    \"turns_5h\": 127,\n    \"turns_7d\": 2840,\n    \"burn_rate_per_min\": 8450.0,\n    \"forecast_full_5h_min\": 105.0,\n    \"forecast_full_7d_min\": null,\n    \"source\": \"api_cache\",\n    \"computed_at\": \"2026-05-03T14:20:00Z\"\n  }\n]\n```\n\n### Data Sources\n\nThe capacity meter reads from two sources (in priority order):\n\n1. **Cached API response** (`~/.cache/claude-usage/usage.json`) — exact numbers matching Claude Code's `/status` output. This file is written by Claude Code when you run `/status` or check limits.\n\n2. **JSONL-based estimation** — fallback when cache is stale or missing. Parses `~/.claude/projects/*/*.jsonl` files and counts tokens using cost-equivalent weighting:\n   - Input tokens: 1.0× weight\n   - Output tokens: ~5× weight (matching API pricing ratio)\n   - Cache read tokens: ~0.1× weight\n   - Cache write tokens: ~0.25× weight\n\nThe JSONL fallback is inherently approximate because the exact weighting formula is proprietary. The cached API response should be preferred whenever available.\n\n### Account Discovery\n\nBy default, scans:\n- `~/.claude` (named \"claude-default\" in output)\n- All `~/.claude-*` directories that contain `.credentials.json`\n\nFor example, if you have `~/.claude` and `~/.claude-work`, both will be scanned and reported separately.\n\n### Exit Codes\n\n| Code | Meaning |\n|------|---------|\n| 0 | Success |\n| 1 | No Claude accounts found |\n\n---\n\n## `agentscribe context`\n\nPre-task priming query for agent workers. `agentscribe reflect`\n\nExport sessions with behavioral metadata for reflection analysis. This is the stable data export API for external reflection tools that analyze agent behavior across sessions.\n\n### Usage\n\n```\nagentscribe reflect <subcommand> [options]\n```\n\n### Subcommands\n\n#### `agentscribe reflect sessions`\n\nExport sessions with behavioral signals, error fingerprints, and config file interactions. When combined with `--json`, outputs a stable, machine-readable schema suitable for programmatic consumption by reflection tools.\n\n```\nagentscribe reflect sessions [options]\n```\n\n##### Options\n\n| Option | Short | Default | Description |\n|--------|-------|---------|-------------|\n| `--since <datetime>` | | all | Only include sessions after this timestamp. ISO 8601 or relative (`7d`, `30d`, `12w`). |\n| `--project <path>` | | all projects | Only include sessions from this project path. |\n| `--outcome <outcome>` | | all | Only include sessions with this outcome (`success`, `failure`, `abandoned`, `unknown`). |\n| `--modified-config-only` | | off | Only include sessions where agent modified config/memory files. |\n| `--read-config-only` | | off | Only include sessions where agent read config/memory files. |\n| `--limit <n>` | `-n` | none | Maximum number of sessions to return. |\n| `--tags <tags>` | `-t` | none | Filter by annotation tags (AND logic: all tags must be present). Can be repeated. |\n| `--json` | | off | Output in stable JSON format (documented below). |\n\n##### Examples\n\n```bash\n# Export last 30 days of sessions as JSON\nagentscribe reflect sessions --since 30d --json\n\n# Only sessions that modified CLAUDE.md or other config files\nagentscribe reflect sessions --modified-config-only --json\n\n# Failed sessions from a specific project\nagentscribe reflect sessions --project ~/myproject --outcome failure --json\n\n# Sessions tagged with \"config-change\" or \"repeated-mistake\"\nagentscribe reflect sessions --tags config-change --tags repeated-mistake --json\n```\n\n##### JSON Output Schema (Stable Contract)\n\nThe `--json` flag outputs a stable, machine-readable schema. **This schema is versioned**: new fields may be added at any time, but existing fields will never be renamed, removed, or retyped without a major version bump.\n\nOutput format: array of `ReflectSession` objects.\n\n```json\n[\n  {\n    \"session_id\": \"string\",\n    \"agent\": \"string\",\n    \"project\": \"string | null\",\n    \"started\": \"string (ISO 8601)\",\n    \"ended\": \"string (ISO 8601) | null\",\n    \"duration_secs\": \"number (u64)\",\n    \"outcome\": \"string\",\n    \"summary\": \"string | null\",\n    \"tags\": [\"string\"],\n    \"model\": \"string | null\",\n    \"tool_call_counts\": {\"string\": \"number (u32)\"},\n    \"re_read_count\": \"number (u32)\",\n    \"bash_failure_count\": \"number (u32)\",\n    \"read_config_files\": [\"string\"],\n    \"modified_config_files\": [\"string\"],\n    \"error_fingerprints\": [\"string\"],\n    \"anti_patterns\": [{\"pattern\": \"string\"}],\n    \"files_touched\": [\"string\"],\n    \"config_changes_after\": [{\"file\": \"string\", \"minutes_after\": \"number (u64)\"}] | null\n  }\n]\n```\n\n###### Field Descriptions\n\n| Field | Type | Nullable | Description |\n|-------|------|----------|-------------|\n| `session_id` | string | no | Session ID in `<agent>/<session-id>` format |\n| `agent` | string | no | Source agent name (plugin name) |\n| `project` | string | yes | Project path, if available |\n| `started` | string | no | Session start timestamp (ISO 8601) |\n| `ended` | string | yes | Session end timestamp (ISO 8601), if available |\n| `duration_secs` | number | no | Session duration in seconds |\n| `outcome` | string | no | Session outcome: `success`, `failure`, `abandoned`, or `unknown` |\n| `summary` | string | yes | Generated summary of the session |\n| `tags` | array | no | \"Bash\": 3}`) |\n| `re_read_count` | number | no | Number of times files were re-read in this session |\n| `bash_failure_count` | number | no | Number of bash commands that returned non-zero exit code |\n| `read_config_files` | array | no | Config/memory files read in this session (CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md, .claude/, memory/, etc.) |\n| `modified_config_files` | array | no | Config/memory files written/edited in this session |\n| `error_fingerprints` | array | no | Error fingerprints found in this session (hashed error signatures) |\n| `anti_patterns` | array | no | Anti-patterns detected in this session (each has `pattern` field) |\n| `files_touched` | array | no | Files touched in this session (any file operation) |\n| `config_changes_after` | array | yes | Config file changes observed after this session (each has `file` and `minutes_after` fields) |\n\n###### Example Output\n\n```json\n[\n  {\n    \"session_id\": \"claude-code/abc123\",\n    \"agent\": \"claude-code\",\n Exit Codes\n\n| Code | Meaning |\n|------|---------|\n| 0 | Success |\n| 1 | Data dir not initialized |\n| 2 | No sessions found matching filters |\n\n---\n\n### Behavioral Signals Schema\n\nThe `BehavioralSignals` struct is computed from session events and stored as a sidecar file (`sessions/<agent>/<session-id>.behavioral.json`). It provides quantitative metrics for reflection analysis.\n\n**File format**: `~/.agentscribe/sessions/<agent>/<session-id>.behavioral.json`\n\n```json\n{\n  \"tool_call_count\": \"number (u32)\",\n  \"tool_call_counts_by_name\": {\"string\": \"number (u32)\"},\n  \"re_read_files\": [\"string\"],\n  \"re_read_count\": \"number (u32)\",\n  \"bash_failure_count\": \"number (u32)\",\n  \"multi_edit_files\": [\"string\"],\n  \"duration_secs\": \"number (u64)\",\n  \"assistant_turn_ratio\": \"number (f32)\",\n  \"read_config_files\": [\"string\"],\n  \"modified_config_files\": [\"string\"],\n  \"cwd_switch_count\": \"number (u32)\"\n}\n```\n\n#### Field Descriptions\n\n| Field | Type | Description |\n|-------|------|-------------|\n| `tool_call_count` | number | Total tool calls in session |\n| `tool_call_counts_by_name` | object | Tool call counts broken down by tool name |\n| `re_read_files` | array | Files read more than once in the same session (re-read pattern) |\n| `re_read_count` | number | Number of re-read events (each duplicate read beyond the first counts as one) |\n| `bash_failure_count` | number | Bash commands that returned non-zero exit code |\n| `multi_edit_files` | array | Files written/edited more than once (possible revert pattern) |\n| `duration_secs` | number | Approximate session duration in seconds (last_ts - first_ts) |\n| `assistant_turn_ratio` | number | Ratio: assistant turns / total turns (0.0 to 1.0) |\n| `read_config_files` | array | Config/memory files read (CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md, .claude/**, .needle/**, memory/, docs/notes/) |\n| `modified_config_files` | array | Config/memory files written/edited |\n| `cwd_switch_count` | number | Number of times agent switched working directory (cwd changes in events) |\n\n#### Config File Patterns\n\nThe following patterns are detected as config/memory files:\n- `CLAUDE.md`, `AGENTS.md`\n- `.claude/**`, `.needle/**`\n- `memory/**`, `docs/notes/**`\n- `MEMORY.md`\n\n#### Example\n\n```json\n{\n  \"tool_call_count\": 8,\n  \"tool_call_counts_by_name\": {\n    \"Read\": 5,\n    \"Bash\": 2,\n    \"Edit\": 1\n  },\n  \"re_read_files\": [\"/home/user/project/CLAUDE.md\"],\n  \"re_read_count\": 1,\n  \"bash_failure_count\": 0,\n  \"multi_edit_files\": [],\n  \"duration_secs\": 900,\n  \"assistant_turn_ratio\": 0.4,\n  \"read_config_files\": [\"/home/user/project/CLAUDE.md\"],\n  \"modified_config_files\": [],\n  \"cwd_switch_count\": 0\n}\n```\n\n---\n\n### Annotation Schema\n\nAnnotations are sidecar files that store metadata tags and notes for sessions, written by reflection tools or humans. They survive re-scraping because they are independent of session data.\n\n**File format**: `~/.agentscribe/sessions/<agent>/<session-id>.annotations.json`\n\n```json\n{\n  \"session_id\": \"string\",\n  \"annotations\": [\n    {\n      \"tag\": \"string\",\n      \"note\": \"string | null\",\n      \"created_at\": \"string (ISO 8601)\",\n      \"created_by\": \"string\"\n    }\n  ]\n}\n```\n\n#### Field Descriptions\n\n| Field | Type | Nullable | Description |\n|-------|------|----------|-------------|\n| `session_id` | string | no | Session ID this annotation store belongs to |\n| `annotations` | array | no | All annotations for this session |\n| `annotations[].tag` | string | no | Free-form tag string (e.g., `led-to-config-change`, `repeated-mistake`) |\n| `annotations[].note` | string | yes | Human-readable note explaining the annotation |\n| `annotations[].created_at` | string | no | When this annotation was created (ISO 8601) |\n| `annotations[].created_by` | string | no | Source of the annotation: `human`, `reflection-tool`, or `agentscribe` |\n\n#### Example\n\n```json\n{\n  \"session_id\": \"claude-code/abc123\",\n  \"annotations\": [\n    {\n      \"tag\": \"led-to-config-change\",\n      \"note\": \"Agent added a new rule to CLAUDE.md after this session\",\n      \"created_at\": \"2026-03-15T11:00:00Z\",\n      \"created_by\": \"reflection-tool\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"tag\": \"repeated-mistake\",\n      \"note\": \"Agent made the same error pattern 3 times before resolving\",\n      \"created_at\": \"2026-03-15T11:05:00Z\",\n      \"created_by\": \"human\"\n    }\n  ]\n}\n```\n\n---\n\n### MCP Tool: `agentscribe_reflect_sessions`\n\n> **Note:** This MCP tool is **not yet implemented**. Configuration Reference\n\nAgentScribe reads configuration from `~/.agentscribe/config.toml`. On systems that support XDG, this can also be placed at `$XDG_CONFIG_DIR/agentscribe/config.toml`. Override with `--config <path>` or the `AGENTSCRIBE_CONFIG` environment variable.\n\nInitialize the default config with:\n\n```bash\nagentscribe config init\n```\n\n---\n\n## `[general]`\n\nGeneral settings.\n\n| Key | Type | Default | Description |\n|-----|------|---------|-------------|\n| `data_dir` | string | `~/.agentscribe` | Root data directory. All session files, the index, plugins, and state are stored here. Supports `~` expansion. |\n| `log_level` | string | `\"info\"` | Log verbosity. One of: `error`, `warn`, `info`, `debug`, `trace`. Affects stderr output from CLI commands. |\n\n```toml\n[general]\ndata_dir = \"~/.agentscribe\"\nlog_level = \"info\"\n```\n\n---\n\n## `[scrape]`\n\nControls how log files are discovered and processed.\n\n| Key | Type | Default | Description |\n|-----|------|---------|-------------|\n| `debounce_seconds` | integer | `5` | Seconds to wait after a file change before scraping (daemon mode). Prevents thrashing during active agent sessions. |\n| `max_session_age_days` | integer | `0` | Ignore sessions older than N days. `0` means no limit — process all sessions. Useful for large historical logs where you only care about recent activity. |\n\n```toml\n[scrape]\ndebounce_seconds = 5\nmax_session_age_days = 0\n```\n\n---\n\n## `[index]`\n\nTantivy full-text index settings.\n\n| Key | Type | Default | Description |\n|-----|------|---------|-------------|\n| `tantivy_heap_size_mb` | integer | `50` | Memory budget in MB for the Tantivy `IndexWriter`. Higher values speed up indexing at the cost of more RAM. Recommended: 50-200 MB depending on available memory. |\n\n```toml\n[index]\ntantivy_heap_size_mb = 50\n```\n\n---\n\n## `[search]`\n\nDefault search behavior.\n\n| Key | Type | Default | Description |\n|-----|------|---------|-------------|\n| `default_max_results` | integer | `10` | Default number of results returned when `--max-results` is not specified. |\n| `default_snippet_length` | integer | `200` | Default maximum character length of content snippets when `--snippet-length` is not specified. These control how sessions are classified as `success`, `failure`, `abandoned`, or `unknown` based on signal scores.\n\n| Key | Type | Default | Description |\n|-----|------|---------|-------------|\n| `user_satisfaction` | integer | `30` | Weight for user satisfaction signals (e.g., \"thanks\", \"LGTM\", \"looks good\"). |\n| `user_frustration` | integer | `-25` | Weight for user frustration signals (e.g., \"no\", \"wrong\", \"revert\", \"undo\"). |\n| `final_edit_write` | integer | `15` | Weight for sessions ending with an Edit/Write tool call (suggests productive output). |\n| `final_error` | integer | `-20` | Weight for sessions ending with an error (tool_result with error exit code). |\n| `unresolved_error` | integer | `-15` | Weight for sessions with unresolved errors in the last assistant turn. |\n| `tool_success` | integer | `10` | Weight for successful tool calls (exit code 0) in the final turns. |\n| `tool_failure` | integer | `-10` | Weight for failed tool calls (non-zero exit code) in the final turns. |\n| `very_short_session` | integer | `-5` | Weight for sessions with very few turns (likely abandoned or trivial). |\n| `help_without_resolution` | integer | `-10` | Weight for sessions where the agent provided help but the user didn't confirm resolution. |\n| `task_completion` | integer | `25` | Weight for explicit task completion signals (e.g., \"done\", \"finished\", \"committed\"). |\n| `success_threshold` | integer | `20` | Minimum score to classify a session as `success`. Sessions scoring above this are marked success. |\n| `failure_threshold` | integer | `-20` | Maximum score to classify a session as `failure`. Sessions scoring below this are marked failure.
